issue: Discovery sweep examined the widely-reported "Port-Gentil LNG plant" (the ~US$983m / 560bn CFA Perenco + Gabon Oil Company investment announced Jul 2025, e.g. Financial Afrik / Energy Capital Power) and confirmed it is the SAME facility as GEM's existing Cap Lopez FLNG Terminal, not a second/distinct terminal. Cap Lopez is the oil-terminal site near Gabon's second city Port-Gentil, so the two names are geographic references to one project. Capacity figures match GEM exactly (0.70 mtpa LNG + ~25,000 t LPG, 137,000 m3 FSU/FSO conversion, Dixstone EPCCI, FID 2024, first production 2026). Not a discovery; recorded so the "$983m Port-Gentil plant" framing is not mistaken for a missing terminal in a future batch.
suggested_action: No new terminal. Optionally, in a future Update batch, add "Port-Gentil" / "Gabon LNG" as known aliases of Cap Lopez FLNG Terminal and confirm the FID year (2024 per LNG Prime; an earlier source cites Feb 2023 technical approval / FID) on the existing GEM row.

terminal_name: Owendo gas-to-power plant (and other Gabon GTP) -- NOT an LNG terminal
issue: Discovery sweep surfaced several Gabon gas-monetization items that are OUT OF SCOPE for the LNG terminals tracker: the 120-125 MW Owendo gas-to-power plant (Gabon Power Company / Wartsila), CNG refuelling infrastructure (Port-Gentil pilot), and Perenco's Batanga LPG plant (online Dec 2023). These are power generation / LPG / CNG, not LNG liquefaction or LNG import-regasification terminals, so none is a discovery candidate.
suggested_action: None for this tracker. Noted to prevent re-surfacing these as LNG-terminal leads in future Gabon sweeps.
